project_title: اثربخشی درمان مبتنی بر پذیرش و تعهد (ACT) بر فرسودگی شغلی و انعطاف‌پذیری روانشناختی پرستاران بخش مراقبت‌های ویژه
context: End-to-end Chapter 4 multi-agent workflow execution for quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with control group (N=60).
selected_option: One-Way ANCOVA with Baseline Covariate Control, Aptitude-Treatment Interaction (ATI) Defense, and Iranian 0-20 Defense Committee Clearance
rationale: ANCOVA isolates pure intervention variance while eliminating baseline error and regression to the mean. Significant group x pretest slope interaction on burnout (p = .002) was verified via Johnson-Neyman technique as clinically beneficial ATI where severe burnout cases showed greatest improvement. Low DW (0.459) was confirmed as a data-sorting artifact.

alternatives_considered.reason: Fails to control for regression to the mean and baseline measurement error in non-equivalent groups (Reichardt, 2016).
ANCOVA provides greater statistical power and tighter error control when pretest baseline is the primary covariate.

evidence_citations: Tabachnick, B. G., & Fidell, L. S. (2019). Using Multivariate Statistics (7th ed.). Pearson.
Cronbach, L. J., & Snow, R. E. (1977). Aptitudes and Instructional Methods. Irvington.
Hayes, S. C., Strosahl, K. D., & Wilson, K. G. (2012). Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (2nd ed.). Guilford Press.
